author: WhyOS-Apps contributors
description:
Keep the codes you show often, such as a Wi-Fi login, a ticket, a
product number or a login for a barcode scanner, and show them on the
badge's screen for a scanner or a phone to read. Control characters
such as Tab and Enter can be part of a code.

Showing a code:
- Choose it in the list and press Enter. The code is as big as the
  screen allows; the screen goes to full brightness and stays on while
  the code shows, up to 10 minutes after the last key.
- Left and Right go to the previous and next code.

Quick code, the list's first row: type a text and see its code at once.
It is not saved; Enter keeps it as a code of the list.

Making a code: the triangle adds one, the cross edits it, and the
square has the other options (show, edit, type, move, delete). A code
has a name for the list, a type and a text of up to 1000 characters.
In the text:
- Tab puts in a TAB, Shift+Enter a CR (LF or CR LF in the settings).
- Ctrl with a letter puts in ^A to ^Z; Ctrl+] is GS.
- The square puts in any other control character, or GS1's FNC1: type
  its name to find it.
- The triangle chooses the type. Next to each type it says what the
  text needs of it: some take digits only, and Code 39 needs a scanner
  with Full ASCII on for lower case and control characters.

Types: QR Code, Data Matrix, Aztec, PDF417, Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13,
UPC-A, ITF and Codabar.

Settings (cloud key): the type of a new code, QR's error correction,
the quiet zone, what Shift+Enter puts in, the text under a barcode and
full brightness.

The codes are stored as plain text on the badge, so do not save
passwords in them.
